lugwrench lubowski.name: Lugwrench Lubowski
lugwrench lubowski.origin: Lugwrench Lubowski is a self-taught mechanic who lives in the impoverished neighborhoods on Yancy Street in New York City. As an young man, he joined "Two-Fisted" Tommie Boyd's incarnation of the Yancy Street Gang which included a diverse membership. He used his skills as a mechanic to help the group hotwire cars. When young drug addicts were going missing on Yancy Street, the gang grudgingly joined up with hated former member, the Fantastic Four's Thing to learn who was taking the addicts and why. Their investigation took them to an abandoned warehouse where they discovered the Fantastic Four's long time foe Dr. Doom was experimenting on the youths in order to develop a cure for drug addiction, however to date the experiments proved fatal. While the Thing battled Dr. Doom, the gang rescued his latest victim Jimmy Sokolowski, and they escaped just moments before Doom set the warehouse to explode. Later, the gang became prime suspects in the murder of young runaway Alison Gaulthing. The gang, having only witnessed the murder, were on the run from the authorities. When the Childwatch Organization hired the young hero named Justice to apprehend them. With the help of the Thing, Justice convinced the Yancy Street Gang to turn themselves in. Realizing that they were only witnesses to the murder, the gang was released from police custody. Later, the gang was involved in a brawl with the rival Nomads gang. The fight was later interrupted when a malfunctioning Doombot went on a rampage on Yancy Street, sending the Yancy Street and Nomad gangs fleeing. The Doombot was eventually taken down by the NYPD's Code: Blue division. Lubowski and the members of his version of the Yancy Street Gang have not been seen since, their subsequent fate is unknown.

luis augustine.name: Luis Augustine
luis augustine.origin: General Luis Augustine was the commander of the Santo Marco Armed Forces. Upon Magneto's departure of Santo Marco, Augustine assumed control of the country, as President and first citizen of the Republic of Santo Marco, plunging it into another era of dictatorship, and prompting the formation by outspoken activist, Carlos Zapatero of the Popular Front for Santo Marco. Mercenary Parnell Jacobs once ran guns for the Augustine of Santo Marco. Tension grew, with television talking about tribal grudges and atrocities on both sides of the conflict. Despite the presence of international observers, including United Nations Blue Helmets, President Augustine had the army gather citizens to stadiums to use a retrofitted Sentinel to gene scan them, separating out everyone from the same tribe as the main rebel leaders, before performing mass killings. Such massacre was foiled by the timely intervention of War Machine. Augustine was later replaced by President Duarte.

luis fernandez.name: Luis Fernandez
luis fernandez.origin: Luis Fernandez was a prisoner held in one of Kang the Conqueror’s detention camps during the occupation of Earth. He was one of two prisoners who attempted an escape by stealing a guard hover-deck alongside Gordon Michaelson. During their escape attempt, Kang’s forces threatened to execute two other prisoners, Constance Burkhalter and Raymond Campbell, if they did not surrender. The escape attempt resulted in the execution of the hostages. After being recaptured, Fernandez was later executed by firing squad along with other prisoners as punishment for the escape attempt.

luis rodriguez.name: Luis Rodriguez
luis rodriguez.origin: Luis Rodriguez was a kid raised in Hell's Kitchen, who chose the life of crime when he joined Carlos LaMuerto's gang. He was given the name "Little Loco". Years later, now leading his own gang, he robbed an old woman of her money and staged her death as a suicide. Defense Attorney Matt Murdock and his law firm investigated and found that Little Loco was the killer. LaMuerto, recently released from prison and working for Murdock on his parole, went to seek justice under his criminal alias "Black Tarantula". Little Loco had LaMuerto shot, but it only annoyed LaMuerto. LaMuerto killed Little Loco and all of his men, and donated the stolen money.

luiz sifuentes.name: Luiz Sifuentes
luiz sifuentes.origin: Luiz Sifuentes was a New York City resident who witnessed the murder of a person in Central Park. When he approached the body of a man who had been shot, he picked up the revolver used as the murder weapon. When he saw Daredevil approaching the scene, he fled, but was tackled by the vigilante and left tied in a tree for the police. Sifuente's case was assigned to Matt Murdock, Daredevil's alter-ego, who defended him in the court. Using his radar sense to detect whether Sifuentes was lying on his history or not, Murdock discovered that Sifuentes was indeed innocent. As Daredevil, Murdock tracked down the people who had shot the man in Central Park and managed to prove Sifuente's innocence.

lukasz.name: Lukasz
lukasz.species: Immortal warrior that fought Boneyard's forces for centuries in the service of Archimage.
lukasz.origin: The Twelve Knights of Archimage served the white magician Archimage for 1500 years against his sworn foe, Boneyard. The Knights were enchanted by the Archimage so that whenever they died, they would return by possessing the body of an adult male, carrying on in his name. Lukasz and his fellow knights were betrayed and destroyed by one of their own. The traitor Thanasi gave Boneyard power over the Archimage by revealing the magician's true name, leading to a massacre of the knights. Lukasz was slain by the mercenary Warstrike using the Sword of Fangs. Archimage managed to save Lukasz, placing him in the body of Eden Blake: a woman with great potential as a sorceress. It took Lukasz a number of years to adjust to life as Eden and develop magic skill. For many months, he dreamed of one day returning to a male body. Lukasz also began communicating with Eden's soul inside her body, and they fell in love. After the death of the Archimage, however, Lukasz began to lament ever getting back to his own body. He arranged for a new male body to be created for him using nanotech, but the traitor Thanasi possessed Eden's body before she could reinhabit it, becoming Necromantra. On the Godwheel, Lukasz defeated Necromantra and drove Thanasi from the body, allowing him and Eden to meet in person for the first time. Thanasi was not done, however. When Lukasz and Eden consummated their relationship, Thanasi possessed one of Eden's eggs, magically ensuring it was fertilized and rapidly came to term overnight. The baby, named Marinna after Lukasz's first wife, was unable to resist Thanasi's possession, and he turned the infant into a new adult host body for himself, becoming Necromantra again. Although Necromantra was defeated, Eden died in the conflict and Lukasz was forced to possess her body again. Becoming Mantra once more, Lukasz was bound by Eden's dying promise to raise and protect her family.

weaknesses: Mantra's spells do not affect iron. Her personal power is weakened if someone uses her true name against her.

luke bergier.name: Luke Bergier
luke bergier.origin: Luke Bergier was an American freelance photojournalist who traveled the world covering news, including wars, with his fiancée Cindy. Luke's sister, Rebecca Bergier, worked as head of operations for the NGO Worldwatch, investigating human rights causes. Luke and Cindy traveled to San Revilla, a Central American country, to cover the civil war there, but had to try to leave the country on a Red Cross flight. While on the government airstrip, the refugees were attacked by the Shadows, the insurgent group that was fighting the San Revilla government by resorting to terrorist attacks. Although the Shadows were led by former Avenger Hawkeye, who opposed the use of lethal force, the troops concealed their murderous acts from him. One of the Shadows' superhuman agents, the super-strong Striker threw Luke and Cindy into a hangar wall, breaking his arm and her neck. Luke was sent to a dilapidated field hospital. By then, Luke had taken several photos, including one that showed Hawkeye inconclusively. Luke was conscious in the hospital, but seriously injured (with too little mobility even to develop his photos), and knew that Cindy had died. Rebecca convinced her coworker James Rhodes (who was secretly the superhero War Machine) to go to San Revilla to help Luke; Worldwatch provided Rhodes with information and equipment. Rhodes found Luke at the hospital. Luke explained to Rhodes what had happened and gave him his camera so Rhodes could develop the photos. Rhodes recommended Luke leave the country on a refugee flight if possible, and if not, he promised to see him again in a few days. Rhodes then developed the photos. Shortly after, Luke traveled to the Preto airstrip to leave the country on a refugee flight. There were only three planes there that were supposed to take off that night; but the Shadows were misinformed to believe Preto was used to ship foreign mercenaries for the government. The Shadows prepared an attack on Preto. Rhodes, as War Machine, discovered the Shadows' operation, saw that Preto was being used to evacuate innocent people, and also discovered that the mysterious and malevolent Advisor had been manipulating the situation in San Revilla to provoke war. War Machine went to Preto to try to stop Hawkeye and the Shadows, but before he could do so, superhuman government agents (Hazzerd, Troubleshooter, and U.S.Agent) arrived with support troops. Although U.S.Agent, also an Avenger, was reluctant to attack a group that included Hawkeye because they trusted the latter's morale, the situation escalated into a fight. However, Hawkeye, U.S.Agent, and War Machine allied themselves to confront the Shadows and government agents and won, thwarting the Advisor's plans and seemingly preventing further conflict in San Revilla. Hawkeye, Luke, U.S.Agent, and War Machine left San Revilla the next afternoon on an American refugee flight. Luke, sad but relieved and hopeful to see his family again, immortalized Hawkeye's smile in a group photo of the three superheroes. Once back in the States, after a week, Rebecca Bergier had the opportunity to thank Rhodes on Worldwatch for saving her brother Luke, after an adventure in which Rhodes actually saved the world but suffered personal losses that motivated him to take a vacation; Rhodes was so busy that Luke hadn't had the chance to do the same in person. Luke temporarily settled in Los Angeles and attended his sister's birthday party with the rest of the Worldwatch team; Rhodes didn't attend, so Luke asked how he was because he hadn't seen him since they left San Revilla.

fields.history: Luke Bergier was an American freelance photojournalist who traveled the world covering news, including wars, with his fiancée Cindy. Luke's sister, Rebecca Bergier, worked as head of operations for the NGO Worldwatch, investigating human rights causes. Luke and Cindy traveled to San Revilla, a Central American country, to cover the civil war there, but had to try to leave the country on a Red Cross flight. While on the government airstrip, the refugees were attacked by the Shadows, the insurgent group that was fighting the San Revilla government by resorting to terrorist attacks. Although the Shadows were led by former Avenger Hawkeye, who opposed the use of lethal force, the troops concealed their murderous acts from him. One of the Shadows' superhuman agents, the super-strong Striker threw Luke and Cindy into a hangar wall, breaking his arm and her neck. Luke was sent to a dilapidated field hospital. By then, Luke had taken several photos, including one that showed Hawkeye inconclusively. Luke was conscious in the hospital, but seriously injured (with too little mobility even to develop his photos), and knew that Cindy had died. Rebecca convinced her coworker James Rhodes (who was secretly the superhero War Machine) to go to San Revilla to help Luke; Worldwatch provided Rhodes with information and equipment. Rhodes found Luke at the hospital. Luke explained to Rhodes what had happened and gave him his camera so Rhodes could develop the photos. Rhodes recommended Luke leave the country on a refugee flight if possible, and if not, he promised to see him again in a few days. Rhodes then developed the photos. Shortly after, Luke traveled to the Preto airstrip to leave the country on a refugee flight. There were only three planes there that were supposed to take off that night; but the Shadows were misinformed to believe Preto was used to ship foreign mercenaries for the government. The Shadows prepared an attack on Preto. Rhodes, as War Machine, discovered the Shadows' operation, saw that Preto was being used to evacuate innocent people, and also discovered that the mysterious and malevolent Advisor had been manipulating the situation in San Revilla to provoke war. War Machine went to Preto to try to stop Hawkeye and the Shadows, but before he could do so, superhuman government agents (Hazzerd, Troubleshooter, and U.S.Agent) arrived with support troops. Although U.S.Agent, also an Avenger, was reluctant to attack a group that included Hawkeye because they trusted the latter's morale, the situation escalated into a fight. However, Hawkeye, U.S.Agent, and War Machine allied themselves to confront the Shadows and government agents and won, thwarting the Advisor's plans and seemingly preventing further conflict in San Revilla. Hawkeye, Luke, U.S.Agent, and War Machine left San Revilla the next afternoon on an American refugee flight. Luke, sad but relieved and hopeful to see his family again, immortalized Hawkeye's smile in a group photo of the three superheroes. Once back in the States, after a week, Rebecca Bergier had the opportunity to thank Rhodes on Worldwatch for saving her brother Luke, after an adventure in which Rhodes actually saved the world but suffered personal losses that motivated him to take a vacation; Rhodes was so busy that Luke hadn't had the chance to do the same in person. Luke temporarily settled in Los Angeles and attended his sister's birthday party with the rest of the Worldwatch team; Rhodes didn't attend, so Luke asked how he was because he hadn't seen him since they left San Revilla.
equipment: Camera.
transportation: Refugee flights.

luke bowie.name: Luke Bowie
luke bowie.origin: Luke Bowie was the head of a gang of robbers. He managed to escape after a robbery at the Manfried Diamond Cutting Institute, in spite of the intervention of the Human Torch and Toro. For the next robbery at the Federal Reserve, Bowie prepared a trap for the Human Torch and Toro that succeeded perfectly in capturing so the pair of heroes. The two heroes, however, managed to free themselves and put themselves in pursuit of the criminals to prevent the theft to the Federal Reserve. During the chase, Bowie died when his car suffered a fatal accident.

lumen.name: Lumen
lumen.origin: The man that became Lumen was one of a trio of hired muscles gathered by the Mad Thinker when he set out to form a new Fantastic Four. Using the equipment owned by Rachna Koul, the Mad Thinker granted himself and the rest of the team powers similar to those of the original Fantastic Four. Lumen possessed the ability to bend light waves, with which he could become invisible. Calling himself Mister Fantastic, the Mad Thinker took his new Fantastic Four to an alternate universe where the Human Torch and The Thing had become stuck during a multiversal journey in the search for their family. The Mad Thinker intended to eliminate them to consolidate his team since he believed they needed to declutter the void left by the Fantastic Four from its remnants. Despite the fact that both the Human Torch and The Thing were powerless, they managed to hold their own against the Thinker's team. Lumen tried to sneak up on the Human Torch, but Johnny noticed him and elbowed him in the face. Lumen was then knocked out by The Thing. After dealing with the remaining members of the Fantastic Four, the Human Torch and The Thing escaped. The duo regained their powers before their second encounter against the new Fantastic Four, and easily defeated the villain and his pretenders. Following the defeat of all the other members, Lumen surrendered without a fight, arguing that rather than a villain, he was just a guy who needed some extra money. Afterwards, the Human Torch and The Thing returned home, taking the Mad Thinker's team with them.
powers: Light Wave Bending: Lumen possesses the ability to bend light waves, which allows him to become invisible. When his powers are out of control, he is capable of distorting the perception of the environment around him as well.

luminesca.name: Luminesca
luminesca.origin: In the late 37th-early 39th century, Luminesca and her younger brother, Ch'vayre, were classified Alpha-level mutants and raised in a gifted gene-caste, where Ch'vayre dreamed of rank and privilege. In their teens, both siblings became Prelates, serving under Apocalypse's second-in-command, Diamanda Nero, enforcing the mutant class' rule and exterminating dissidents. However, when Apocalypse became debilitated, burning through host bodies faster and faster, Nero assumed much of his power and position, and Luminesca began to visibly resent her authority. Combating the dissident Clan Askani, newly founded by time-traveling Rachel Summers, Nero unleashed the humanoid virus Plague, but ensured that Luminesca and Ch'vayre were within its range as well. Luminesca died, but Rachel nullified the pathogen in time to save Ch'vayre's life.
powers: Luminesca was classified as an Alpha-Level Mutant with the power to fire blasts of light from her hands .

lump warpies.name: Lump (Warpies)
lump warpies.origin: Lump is a member of the Cherubim, which is a group of Warpies who were being used by the R.C.X.. R.C.X. head Peter intended for them to be trained to become a superhuman army. Fearing for the safety of their charges if the plans of their superior went ahead, several R.C.X. agents, led by Agents Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, spirited the children away from the abandoned the agency was housing the Warpies at. They took them to Braddock Manor to enlist the aid of Captain Britain, figuring that he could lend them much needed protection, both physical and politically. However, the agents' decision to not fully inform the hero of their situation meant he was reluctant to help, and while they argued, the Cherubim were released from their van by Meggan. They fought Captain Britain and his allies, Betsy Braddock and Captain UK, but were swiftly overpowered and the Cherub Whirlwind was killed. In the confusion afterwards the Cherubim went rogue and the other Warpies moved into Braddock Manor. The Cherubim soon found themselves in London hoping to find a place for themselves there. However, what the found instead was another group of Warpies known as the Parasites led by Uncle Lex. Uncle Lex sought to use the Warpies for his own purposes including petty thievery. The Cherubim eventually parted company with the Parasites when one of their members, Snap was killed by a bus. The Cherubim was appalled by the lack of concern by the Parasites for their fallen comrade they decided to leave. Uncle Lex refused to let them go and after a brief confrontation with them, the Cherubim departed their company. At some point after this, the Cherubim once again became members of the R.C.X. and went to live at Cloud Nine under the direct supervision of Agent Peter, who sent them out to capture Captain Britain and Meggan and bring them to him at Cloud Nine. Lump and the other members of the Cherubim followed Mastermind when he attempted to conquer Otherworld. He and all the other members of the Cherubim lost their powers there and were turned back into normal humans.
powers: Currently none, all of the Warpies were depowered by Captain Britain on Otherworld using the Sword of Might. {{Navigation

luna depaula.name: Luna DePaula
luna depaula.origin: Operator (and possibly owner) of Grind Stone Café in Salem Center, New York State. She is also a lesbian. She was attracted to Dani Moonstar for a time. Dani in turn introduced Luna to Xuân Cao Mạnh (which Xuân found mildly offensive), but no romance seemed to spark from it. Later same night, Luna was attacked and robbed by Surge. When Surge had recovered she began to work at the Grind Stone Café after school to repay Luna the money she stole. It is very likely that she was killed during Kimura's attack on X-23 and Mercury when the Grind Stone Café was bombed.

lunatik mercenary.name: Lunatik (Mercenary)
lunatik mercenary.origin: left|thumb|143px|A young Lunatik Lunatik was a 600 million year old constantly mutating organism from the planet Wy'nkar, with little morals and a taste for mayhem. ===Origin=== Lunatik had consumed all life on his own planet before escaping on a spaceship sent there by the Interstellar Church of Perpetual Annoyance. He became a mercenary partnered with Skreet, who was the acting Space Pope. Lunatik turned Skreet over to the authorities after she demanded half the money for various jobs the two performed together, but Lunatik himself was also captured and was placed under arrest. ===Crash landing and alliance=== As Lunatik was being transported to the Kyln for trial and imprisonment, the ship suffered a breakdown and crashed on Earth somewhere in the Alaskan wilderness. The crash appeared to have caused a heavy amount of injury, as Lunatik mutated into a newer form with different hair and eyes, and was smaller and much weaker. Lunatik formed an alliance with other survivors of the crash: Paibok and the Blood Brothers. The quartet rounded up people from the local town to help salvage the crashed ship, but Lunatik took too much pleasure in killing any of them that got out of line. ===Drax the Destroyer=== When the Blood Brothers decided to brawl against another survivor, Drax the Destroyer, Lunatik helped Paibok kill Drax to end the conflict, crushing Drax's head. However, Drax did not stay dead for long, and reincarnated in a less powerful but much more cunning and ruthless form. He tracked down the others, killed one of the two Blood Brothers, and decapitated Lunatik. Knowing that Lunatik would eventually heal once his head and body got back together, Drax finished the job by crushing Lunatik's head, telling him to greet Mephisto on the other side.
abilities: Lunatik was a formidable combatant, having had millions of years of experience in numerous forms of . While he preferred hand to hand fighting, he was also a with a number of advanced firearms.

lunatik tyrk fragment.name: Lunatik (Tyrk Fragment)
lunatik tyrk fragment.origin: Lunatik was a mysterious vigilante who operated at the grounds of the Empire State University and the University's vicinity. He attacked persons who violated either laws or rules, no matter how insignificant the violated rule was. He obviously wanted to punish criminals, but could not tell the difference between drug dealers and litterbugs. He would severely beat up violators, in some cases resulting in their deaths. Horace Ledger, friend of Dollar Bill, was badly beaten by Lunatik when he tried to come to Valkyrie's aid. The killings committed by Lunatik regularly made headlines in New York City-based newspapers. On one occasion, Lunatik apprehended a 14-year-old girl who was shoplifting. He proceeded to kill the shoplifter. The Defenders decided to set up a trap for Lunatik, by placing a Spider-Man statue at the grounds of the University. They expected Lunatik to investigate a statue honoring a wanted man like Spider-Man. The Defenders teamed up with Spider-Man for the mission. Lunatik defeated them all and then escaped.
weapons: The Lunatik's main weapon is a metallic staff, which he uses to attack and beat up opponents.

fields.notes: According to the complicated origin story of the character, the extra-dimensional ruler Arisen Tyrk attempted to flee the Other Realm when facing threats to his life. His attempt to cross a damaged extra-dimensional portal, created several different fragments of Tyrk and scattered them across dimensions. Four fragments of Tyrk ended up on Earth. One fragment of Tyrk was sentient, intelligent, and normal-looking. He became Harrison Turk, a drama professor at the Empire State University. Another fragment became the original Lunatik. This fragment was driven by a twisted sense of righteousness, and became a vigilante. He wanted to punish evil-doers, but lacked the rationality to distinguish between serious crimes and misdemeanors. He violently attacked people for the slightest breaking of a law or rule. Two other fragments were driven by different aspects of Tyrk's personality, but looked up to the original Lunatik. They also adopted the identity of the Lunatik, resulting in three different Lunatiks running around. Each looking identical, but acting in different ways. Harrison Turk became aware of his fellow fragments and acted to protect them, providing them with refuge from their foes and shelter in his apartment. The fragments have since been reabsorbed by the original Arisen Tyrk, who was left inert following his last battle. A missing fragment using the Lunatik identity was reportedly located and killed by the mercenary called Lunatik, who considered him a competitor. Lunatik has been able to ambush Spider-Man, without the latter's Spider-Sense warning him. Lunatik typically speaks by quoting songs, films, television shows, and commercials. lunk morton.name: Lunk Morton
lunk morton.origin: Lunk Morton and Wyoming Bates were two outlaws who stalked the Two-Gun Kid while he was riding along a trail, who were trying to make a name for themselves for taking out the Two-Gun Kid. They shoot the Kid in the arm, making their presence known and stating their intentions. Wounded the Kid dived for cover and patched up his wounds. He agreed to come out to face the outlaws, Lunk tells Wyoming to sneak around and attack the Kid from behind. However when Wyoming tries to shoot the Kid from behind, Two-Gun dives down and the bullet strikes Lunk.

lupa lupoff.name: Lupa Lupoff
lupa lupoff.origin: Lupa Lupoff was a communist spy active in the 1950s. She was also her employers' assassin to eliminate those who failed in their missions. Her identity as the Executioner was a secret to all those but her employers and those she eliminated; not even her husband Arnold was aware of her secret role. In 1954, Lupa and Arnold were sent to Las Vegas, Nevada where they were assigned to steal the plans for an atomic trigger for a new atomic cannon being developed by American scientist Jim Slade. To this end, Lupa romanced Slade and began dating him in order to get close enough to the secret plans. However with news that Captain America and Bucky being at the base put the fear in Arnold that the Executioner would come to eliminate him for failing in his mission. Lupa pretended to be afraid to maintain her cover and the two plotted to get the plans that night. When Lupa failed to seduce the secrets out of Jim while out for dinner, Arnold drugged his drink and they fled in their car for the desert. Unknown to them, Captain America and Bucky had already learned the true identity of Jim's new girlfriend and were at the scene. Bucky managed to climb aboard the car but Captain America was held up by an attack from an army of communist spies. Out in the desert Lupa and Arnold tied Jim to a cactus and demanded he reveal where the secret plans are kept. Bucky then attacked but he too was captured. When Captain America finally caught up he easily beat Arnold in a fight. Deeming the mission a failure, Lupa revealed to Arnold that she was the Executioner and shot her husband dead. Then, to the shock of Captain America and Bucky, Lupa then turned the gun on herself and committed suicide having deemed her mission a failure as well.
